description.value: The study investigated the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying verbal fluency impairment in fv-FTD and SD using semantic and phonemic fluency tasks, neuropsychological assessment, and resting-state FDG PET correlations.

spans.text: The aim of this study was to gain a better understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying verbal fluency impairment in the frontal variant of frontotemporal dementia (fv-FTD) and in semantic dementia (SD).

description.value: The study compared fv-FTD patients, SD patients, and healthy elderly subjects using neuropsychological testing and resting FDG PET.

spans.text: We also studied a group of 18 healthy elderly subjects, selected to match the fv-FTD and SD patients in terms of age, sex and education level.
